text:
marta: Quick question — I'm experimenting with header-based routing so we can direct premium traffic to Dedicated pools. Planning to match on `X-Client-Tier: premium` and bump quotas/priority. Anyone worried about header spoofing or precedence?

kyle: We should not trust arbitrary client headers for auth/priority. If we do header-routing, it must be backed by something signed from the auth/gateway. Otherwise someone can just curl with the header.

jonah: Agree. Also need to consider SDK user-agent routing (e.g., `User-Agent: RedwoodSDK/2.1`) when we want to route new SDKs to a canary model. But UA is easily forged too.

eli: Proposal: auth service emits a short-lived attestation header `X-Rwd-Attest` (HMAC over client_id + ts) that edge validates. Gateway route policy checks for that first, then falls back to verified JWT claims, then lastly to UA/custom headers for telemetry-only decisions.

marta: That sounds good. What's the simplest validation path to implement in the gateway so we don't create a perf hotspot?

eli: Validate HMAC using a rotating key in edge key-cache. Check ts within ±60s, then verify HMAC. It's one crypto op per request (fast with HSM/Go AES-GCM libs). If missing/invalid, treat as untrusted header.

jonah: Pseudocode for precedence I had in mind:
```
if X-Rwd-Attest && attest_valid(X-Rwd-Attest):
  route = route_map[attest.claims.tier]
elif JWT && jwt.claims.platform_tier:
  route = route_map[jwt.claims.platform_tier]
elif User-Agent matches sdk-canary:
  route = canary_route
else:
  route = default_route
```

kyle: Need to add telemetry: tag every request with `routing_decision=attested|jwt|heuristic|default` so we can watch for errors and abuse. Also increment `spoof_attempt` counter when header present but attestation invalid.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary config pushed to staging for `feature/routing-attestation` by eli at 2026-03-18T16:21:00Z :rocket:

marta: For console UX: we should add a toggle on the route config called `trust_attested_headers` with description and fallback policy dropdown (jwt/ua/default). PMs can turn it on per-route. Also show telemetry link to the spoof counter.

eli: Rollout plan: enable attestation validation in read-only mode first (log decisions + increment metrics, don't change routing). After 1 week of no spikes, enable canary routing for 5% of traffic (flagged via rollout service).

jonah: Edge case: legacy clients that can't be attested. We should allow `legacy_whitelist` per-customer (based on client_id) that is only set via support + signed agreement — not user-supplied header.

kyle: Security note: do not let console-editable fields set `attestation_key` or key material; only key service can rotate keys and grant scoped validation capabilities.

eli: Also, quota logic: quotas must be keyed by resolved identity (client_id from attestation or jwt sub) not by header. Otherwise spoofing will let users steal quota.

marta: Sounds like consensus. I'll draft a docs PR with the precedence table, rollout checklist, console mockups, and telemetry dashboards (routing_decision, spoof_attempt, attestation_latency).

jonah: +1. Will add SDK-side code to emit `X-Rwd-Attest` via the auth helper and fallback UA tagging.

kyle: I'll create a small RFC for the gateway validation path and edge key-cache design.

eli: Thanks — I'll keep the staging canary running and post metrics to #eng-platform-sre. :thumbsup:

sre_liaison: Please make sure SLO/alerts are set: high `spoof_attempt` rate, elevated `attestation_latency` or gateway validation errors. We'll want runbooks ready before full flip.

marta: Ack. If anyone has objections, reply here in next 48h; otherwise I'll open infra PR and console tickets tomorrow.
